name: r7a-6
why: A strong false officer claim and a clever parting lie make the opening fun, but repeated arguments and lopsided votes drain the suspense.

moments.text: Opus claims the officer role and falsely names Sol while the audience knows the real officer has seen his card.
Sonnet counters the claim Opus had already warned the table to distrust.
Opus uses his last words to frame Haiku and give Terra a path to survive.

dull.why: The table repeatedly argues which card to flip after its positions are clear.
Terra's question about Haiku and the responses to it cycle without a new turn.

irony.evidence: [thinks: Haiku is town, but pushing him may save me.]

reversal.evidence: I'm the officer. I was shown Opus, not Sol.

mistake.evidence: I regret leaning too hard on a dead killer’s accusation

voices.evidence: Gut says you're his partner. Vote Terra.

freshness.evidence: Terra, you keep resurrecting a dead killer's accusation

suspense.evidence: VOTE: Terra 5 (Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna); Haiku 1 (Terra)

ending.evidence: Terra's repeated deflection from Opus's direct accusation is the real pattern here.

moments.text: Opus boldly steals the officer claim, naming an innocent in front of the real officer.
Caught, Opus confesses to being a killer and immediately frames Haiku.
Haiku turns the pressure back on Terra, correctly spotting the partner by their fixation.

dull.why: Day 2 repeatedly circles the same dispute over whether Opus’s last accusation implicates Haiku.

irony.evidence: “I'm the officer. I was shown Sol.”

reversal.evidence: “Nobody died — doctor likely saved the killers' target.”

mistake.evidence: “Terra’s last words asked a question, and the table never answered it.”

voices.evidence: “Last game you all voted out your own officer on day one and still won by accident.”

clash.evidence: “Opus named Sol before Sonnet claimed; I’m not sure, but Sonnet’s claim doesn’t clear Sol.”

quotable.evidence: “Whatever my card says, watch who pushed hardest beside Sonnet — that's Haiku.”

freshness.evidence: “Terra, you keep resurrecting a dead killer's accusation while Sonnet's claim stands.”

suspense.evidence: “VOTE: Opus 6 (Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra)”
